prompt: bia is Owner of `shop-prod`. *Allowed locations*, set to Brazil, is assigned on `mg-shop` with `deny`. She asks for a machine in `southcentralus`. What happens?
hint: Is policy about who asks?

choices.text: It is created, because Owner may do anything in the subscription
choices.why: Owner is a permission. Policy judges the resource, whoever asks.

choices.text: It is created and marked non-compliant
choices.why: That is `audit`. This assignment uses `deny`.

choices.text: It is refused
choices.why: Right. The rule is about Texas, not about bia.

choices.text: It is created in `brazilsouth` instead
choices.why: Policy never moves a request to another region.

prompt: What is the difference between a policy definition and a policy assignment?
hint: One says what, the other says where.

choices.text: A definition is built-in and an assignment is custom
choices.why: Both definitions and assignments exist in either flavour.

choices.text: The definition is the rule; the assignment puts it on a scope
choices.why: Right. One definition can be assigned many times with different parameters.

choices.text: A definition applies to resources and an assignment to identities
choices.why: Neither applies to identities; that is role-based access.

choices.text: An assignment is a definition that has already run once
choices.why: An assignment is a resource of its own, not a run.

prompt: Why is the id of *Allowed locations*, `e56962a6-...`, the same in every tenant?
hint: Look at where the id starts.

choices.text: It is not: the GUID differs per subscription
choices.why: A built-in's GUID is fixed; that is why a template can name it.

choices.text: Every tenant copies it from GitHub on creation
choices.why: GitHub is where it is published, not where tenants get it.

choices.text: Policy ids are derived from the display name
choices.why: The name is a GUID; nothing is derived from the title.

choices.text: It is a built-in, defined once by Microsoft above every tenant
choices.why: Right. Its id starts at `/providers/`, with no subscription.

prompt: The shop writes a custom definition about resource groups and gives it `"mode": "Indexed"`. It is assigned, it reports, and no resource group is ever refused. Why?
hint: What does `Indexed` look at?

choices.text: `Indexed` only sees types with tags and a location, and skips groups
choices.why: Right. A rule about groups needs mode `All`.

choices.text: Resource groups are exempt from every policy
choices.why: Microsoft ships a built-in for resource groups, in mode `All`.

choices.text: The assignment needs a managed identity
choices.why: Only `modify` and `deployIfNotExists` need one.

choices.text: Custom definitions cannot use `deny`
choices.why: They can; the shop's own uses it.

prompt: In a policy rule, `allOf` means every condition must hold, and `___` means at least one must.
hint: The two combine conditions, like and/or.

prompt: *Allowed locations* is assigned on `mg-shop`. Which of these does it govern?
hint: An assignment holds at its scope and below.

choices.text: Only resources created directly in `mg-shop`
choices.why: Resources are not created in management groups; they live in subscriptions below.

choices.text: Only the subscriptions that existed on the day it was assigned
choices.why: Next year's subscription under `mg-shop` is governed too.

choices.text: The tenant root group and everything in the tenant
choices.why: It reaches down, never up.

choices.text: Every resource in every subscription under `mg-shop`
choices.why: Right. Including those created later.

prompt: The owner of `shop-staging` dislikes a deny assigned on `mg-shop`. What can they do from inside their subscription?
hint: Can something below switch off a rule from above?

choices.text: Assign the same definition with `disabled` at the subscription
choices.why: That adds a second assignment; the first still applies.

choices.text: See it, and nothing else
choices.why: Right. A way out is written into the assignment or an exemption, above.

choices.text: Delete the assignment, since it applies to their resources
choices.why: The assignment lives on `mg-shop`, out of their reach.

choices.text: Move the subscription out of `mg-shop`
choices.why: Moving a subscription between management groups is not the subscription owner's call.

prompt: A subscription denies everything outside `brazilsouth`; a resource group inside it denies everything outside `brazilsoutheast`. Where can a resource in that group be created?
hint: Each assignment is evaluated on its own.

choices.text: Nowhere
choices.why: Right. Cumulative most restrictive: each region fails one of the two rules.

choices.text: In either of the two regions
choices.why: Each region is denied by one of the two assignments.

choices.text: In `brazilsoutheast`, because the nearer rule wins
choices.why: No rule wins; both apply.

choices.text: In `brazilsouth`, because the subscription's rule is higher
choices.why: Being higher does not override; both are evaluated.

prompt: Why does the compiled `policy.bicep` hold `[[parameters('effect')]` with two brackets?
hint: Two evaluators read that string.

choices.text: A bug in Bicep 0.48.1 that doubles the bracket
choices.why: It is deliberate escaping, documented behaviour.

choices.text: To make Resource Manager evaluate it twice
choices.why: Resource Manager evaluates it zero times; it strips one bracket and stores the text.

choices.text: So Resource Manager stores it as text for Policy to evaluate
choices.why: Right. One bracket is removed at deployment, and Policy reads the rest each time the rule runs.

choices.text: Because policy parameters must start with two brackets
choices.why: In the stored definition it has one, as in the built-in.

prompt: The shop's environment-tag assignment uses `enforcementMode: 'DoNotEnforce'`. What does that give the shop?
hint: How should a new rule start?

choices.text: A rule that applies to new resources only
choices.why: Every deny applies to new requests only; this is about not denying at all.

choices.text: A report of what the rule would refuse, refusing nothing
choices.why: Right. Evaluate first, enforce once the report is understood.

choices.text: A rule that the owner of each subscription can switch off
choices.why: Nothing below can switch an assignment off.

choices.text: A cheaper assignment, billed at half the price of an enforced one
choices.why: Enforcement mode has nothing to do with billing.

prompt: At most how many characters may the name of a policy assignment at a management group have?
hint: `shop-environment-tag` meets it with four to spare.

prompt: Match each way of loosening a policy to what it is.
hint: Two of them are written into or beside the assignment.

pairs.right: one scope excused from one assignment, until a date

prompt: Which effect lets the resource be created and marks it non-compliant?
hint: The reporting family.

choices.text: `deny`
choices.why: That refuses the request.

choices.text: `modify`
choices.why: That changes the request before it is carried out.

choices.text: `disabled`
choices.why: That does nothing at all.

choices.text: `audit`
choices.why: Right. Created, and reported.

prompt: Put these effects in the order Azure Policy runs them when a request arrives.
hint: A rule switched off costs nothing; a change can make a deny unnecessary.
trap: `modify` comes before `deny`: a request given the missing tag should not then be refused for missing it.

prompt: The built-in *Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing* lists the Contributor role in its rule. Who gets that role?
hint: An effect that acts needs somebody to act.

choices.text: Whoever creates the resource
choices.why: The creator's permissions decide whether they may ask, not what Policy may change.

choices.text: Microsoft's support team, for remediation
choices.why: Nobody at Microsoft acts on your resources for a policy.

choices.text: The assignment's managed identity
choices.why: Right. `modify` acts as that identity, at the assignment's scope.

choices.text: Nobody: a built-in already has every permission
choices.why: A built-in is a definition; it acts through an identity like any other.

prompt: *Allowed locations* with `deny` is assigned on a subscription that already has a machine in Texas. What happens to the machine?
hint: When does a deny act?

choices.text: It keeps running, marked non-compliant
choices.why: Right. A deny acts on requests; what exists is reported.

choices.text: It is deleted at the next 24-hour evaluation
choices.why: Evaluation reports; it never deletes.

choices.text: It is moved to `brazilsouth` by a remediation task
choices.why: Remediation exists for `modify` and `deployIfNotExists`, and no effect relocates a machine.

choices.text: It is stopped within five minutes
choices.why: Five minutes is when the assignment applies, and applying stops nothing.

prompt: What is an initiative in Azure Policy?
hint: The API calls it a policy set definition.

choices.text: A remediation task started by hand
choices.why: That is remediation, a different thing.

choices.text: A definition that runs before any other
choices.why: Order is decided by effect, not by grouping.

choices.text: A group of definitions assigned and reported as one
choices.why: Right. Microsoft's regulatory benchmarks are built-in initiatives.

choices.text: An assignment that applies to a whole tenant
choices.why: Scope belongs to assignments; an initiative is a kind of definition.

prompt: Assignments are evaluated again once every ___ hours in the standard cycle.
hint: A day.

prompt: The shop wants every new storage account to have a diagnostic setting, created automatically when it is missing. Which effect fits?
hint: A related resource deployed if it is missing.

choices.text: `auditIfNotExists`
choices.why: That reports the missing setting and creates nothing.

choices.text: `deployIfNotExists`
choices.why: Right. It needs the assignment's managed identity and a role to do it.

choices.text: `modify`
choices.why: `modify` changes the request's own properties, such as tags; it does not create a second resource.

choices.text: `append`
choices.why: `append` adds fields to the request; it creates nothing beside it.

prompt: Which of these did the lab show without an Azure account? Choose all that apply.
hint: What came from GitHub and from Bicep, and what was refused?

choices.text: The rule of a built-in definition
choices.why: Right. Read from the GitHub copy.

choices.text: The ARM template of an assignment at a management group
choices.why: Right. `az bicep build`.

choices.text: A deny refusing a resource in Texas
choices.why: That needs Resource Manager; it was taught from the documentation.

choices.text: The compliance report of `shop-prod`
choices.why: Compliance lives in Azure; the scan request was refused.

choices.text: The role a `modify` built-in asks for
choices.why: Right. Contributor's GUID, in the rule.

prompt: A team wants test machines in Texas while production stays in Brazil, both under `mg-shop`. What change keeps *Allowed locations* on `mg-shop` honest?
hint: The way out is written above, not done below.

choices.text: Assign *Allowed locations* again on the test subscription with Texas in the list
choices.why: The `mg-shop` assignment would still deny Texas; rules add up.

choices.text: Switch the assignment to `audit` for everybody
choices.why: That loosens production too, which nobody asked for.

choices.text: Give the team Owner on `mg-shop` so they can bypass it
choices.why: Owner does not bypass policy.

choices.text: An exemption for the test subscription, with a reason and an end date
choices.why: Right. Written down, visible, and it expires; `notScopes` is the other honest route.
